# Synthetics and Working Joes [italic]From ColonyPedia, the free encyclopedia of the frontier. This article is about artificial persons. For the frozen dinner brand, see Synthetic Steak.[/italic]
A [bold]synthetic[/bold], properly an [bold]artificial person[/bold], is a manufactured human-shaped machine built to work alongside people. The two great families on the frontier are the high-end synthetics of Hyperdyne Systems and Weyland-Yutani, which can pass for human, and the Working Joe line by Seegson, which cannot and does not try.
## THE WORKING JOE The Working Joe was released by Seegson as a cheap, tireless and fully obedient labourer. It has a rubber face, a calm voice and a single expression, chosen in testing as the one least likely to cause complaints. It is found on most Seegson-serviced colonies, mopping, lifting, sorting and reminding colonists that running in the corridors is not permitted.
Joes are bound by their safety directives, which forbid them from harming a human. Seegson stresses that these directives cannot be overridden. Seegson has issued fourteen patches to the directives that cannot be overridden.
## HIGH-END SYNTHETICS Hyperdyne and Weyland-Yutani models serve as science officers, medics and executive staff. They are strong, quick, patient and very good at chess. Many colonists say they cannot tell a modern synthetic from a person, which the makers present as a selling point and colonists present as a concern.
## TERMINOLOGY Synthetics generally prefer the term artificial person. Working Joes have no stated preference. When asked, a Working Joe will reply that it is here to help, which ColonyPedia has decided to treat as a preference.
## CONTROVERSY An earlier version of this article claimed that some synthetics carry orders from their makers that override the wishes of their crew. That section was removed after a request from a legal department. ColonyPedia would like to state that we did not say which legal department.
